item.title: Composer Without PHP: Embedding vivacity in ePHPm
item.description: The pitch for ePHPm is one binary in place of php-fpm, nginx and Redis. There was always a hole in it though. To deploy a PHP app you still need to run composer install, and that drags PHP and composer.phar back onto the box, or into the container build, just for that one step. ephpm composer install now runs a pure-Rust, Composer-compatible installer called vivacity inside the ePHPm binary. One binary serves the app and installs its dependencies, and on Windows that works with no PHP installed at all. Getting it right took five upstream PRs, a fork, a docs rewrite that took back claims we’d already made, and teaching ephpm to pretend to be php.

item.title: Calling Rust From PHP Without a Socket, Part 2: Making Existing Code Use It
item.description: Part 1 covered the plumbing: ePHPm registers ephpm_kv_* and ephpm_db_* functions that call straight into Rust, and a cache read through one costs about a tenth of a microsecond instead of a loopback round trip. That’s nice and also useless on its own, because nobody is going to rewrite their WordPress object cache or their Laravel cache store around a function called ephpm_kv_set(). Applications talk to Redis through phpredis or Predis, to the cache through PSR-6/16 or wp_cache_*, and to the database through wpdb, mysqli, Eloquent or DBAL.
